Cloud GUI Remake — the terminal wave: run the predicate LAST, take the verdict, end the epic

Living wave Paper for the Cloud GUI Remake epic (bp task task-47bc4168392dec17, phase 5). Root task this wave: gr-p5r5-successor-seal (the terminal run itself, 13 frozen acceptance criteria). Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-gui-remake-charter.md — the epic's law, round-10 DECIDE section at GR142-GR152. Prior wave Paper: cloud-gui-remake-wave-2026-07-20-seal-r10. This is the EIGHTH seal attempt, and it is chartered to be the LAST — not by forcing a green, but by taking whatever the frozen predicate returns as terminal.

Where this wave stands (updated by each phase)
Strategize has set the direction and OPENED this Paper. Digest appends the survey digest + verify plan BEFORE the verifiers fly. Decide appends the decisions + wave plan BEFORE the builders fly. Review closes this Paper as the debrief. Someone opening this mid-wave sees exactly where it stands. Fan-out workers NEVER write this Paper — they write their own bp task; the next Fable folds their reports in.

The wish, verbatim

MODEL CONSTRAINT (hard): Fable 5 is spend-limited — every phase runs on Opus/Sonnet, and Decide MUST set builder_model:'opus' for EVERY slice, never 'fable'. — THIS CYCLE: END THE CLOUD GUI REMAKE. Everything the seal needs is now on main: the frozen predicate, the clause-(b) registered commits (#5078), the 62-row disposition census (#5079), and the round-10 DECIDE charter (#5089). Run the predicate LAST, once, and take the verdict — SEAL or NO SEAL. Build NO seventh instrument. Root task: gr-p5r5-successor-seal (0/13).

Ground truth — re-verified at Strategize (2026-07-21)

The wish's four 'everything is on main' claims were checked at L2 against origin/main and the live ledger. THREE hold; ONE does not, and that gap is the wave's real work.

VERIFIED on origin/main: (1) Clause (b) is SATISFIABLE — the predicate's KNOWN_DEFECTS all carry commit '0261ace15' (seal-predicate.mjs:86/92/98), and git merge-base --is-ancestor 0261ace15 origin/main exits 0. This landed via #5060 (gr-p5r8), not the PR number the wish cites, but the SUBSTANCE is on main. (2) The round-10 DECIDE section (GR142-GR152) is on main via #5089. (3) The named successor cloud-console-hardening-epic resolves PUBLISHED, top-level, open, with its six-band charter and now 7 children (all gr-bl-* backlog rows). The second-successor hazard gr-p5r3-successor-epic reads done. There is exactly ONE forwarding address.

The one wish-claim that does NOT hold — this is the wave's work
The '62-row disposition census (#5079)' is NOT yet a written artifact. The charter carries the census PLAN (line 1297, 'Ledger disposition — the census this wave ships') but NOT the 62 individual disposition rows. The census slice gr-p5r10-census is still lifecycle=open at 7/8. And the moves have not happened: the live roster under the epic root reads 140 children {done:80, open:59, in_progress:1}, and the successor has ZERO survivors re-parented (its 7 children are all backlog rows, not forwarded residue). So clause (a) will fail hard (~60 orphans) until this wave executes the move-set. The census and the moves ARE the deliverable; the exit code is only the signature.

The direction — EXECUTE AND DISCLOSE, then END

This is NOT a design wave. There is no new Kinsta/Vercel surface to shape; the CODE that ships the console already shipped. The whole point, learned the hard way across six failed seals, is the META-FINDING: each round spawned a new instrument and the seal receded by one instrument per round. A seventh widening is not rigor — it is how an epic never closes. THIS WAVE BUILDS NO NEW INSTRUMENT. It executes the fully-prepared round-10 plan and takes the verdict.

The finished state this wave delivers: (a) the 62-row disposition census is WRITTEN into the charter — every live row either closed on a named merge SHA or forwarded to the ONE successor with a named band, zero unnamed remainder; (b) the move-set is executed via bp task move (60 orphans to cloud-console-hardening-epic, self-orphan gr-p5r5-successor-seal re-parented LAST, the two in-roster human gates forwarded, cloud-console-billing-live-gate left untouched under its true owner); (c) the frozen predicate runs LAST, ONCE, atomically, by the SAME agent that finished the ledger, from the repo root, with --successor cloud-console-hardening-epic and OVERFLOW_GUARD_PORT set to a verified-free port; (d) its VERBATIM stdout + stderr + exit code + ISO stamp + roster count is recorded in the charter as the TERMINAL ARTIFACT, beside the census and the roster delta — WHICHEVER WAY IT EXITS.

The verdict is disclosure, not rename. The predicate can only measure 'does this row's parent equal the successor id' — a chartered successor and an empty junk-drawer pass it identically. That is why the CENSUS is the real deliverable and the exit code is only the signature. SEAL (exit 0) closes the epic as CODE-sealed. NO SEAL (non-zero) hands the epic to the named successor — a fully pre-authorised, terminal ending. Either way the epic ENDS this wave. There is no round 11.

THE CROWN IS DARK — 'seal' means CODE seal only
PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS is unset on the control plane (re-proven live: /v1/me gives platform_operator:false; /v1/operator/warm-pool gives 403). The operator console shipped fully built and remains UNREACHABLE. No commit can set an unset prod env var. The terminal artifact must say this in plain words: a green exit code is a CODE seal, not a live-operator seal. gr-ops-platform-admin-emails, cloud-console-billing-live-gate, and gr-backlog-qr-live-scan-proof are the three permanent human gates — labelled, forwarded, and disclosed, never swept.

The direction debate — the rivals weighed

RIVAL A — 'Add the rigor that finally earns the green' (the seventh-instrument trap). If the predicate risks a substantive NO SEAL from a real remaining defect, use this wave to also fix it, or to widen the census/measurement so the seal is 'truly' earned. REJECTED: this IS the failure mode that killed six rounds. GR140/GR146 draw the line — widening what the predicate MEASURES (KNOWN_DEFECTS, clauses, thresholds) is the forbidden move; a substantive NO SEAL is not a bug to engineer around, it IS the verdict, and the named successor is the honest ending. A wave that plans to prevent NO SEAL has already lost.

RIVAL B — 'Execute exactly the prepared plan; the census is the deliverable, the exit code is the signature' (WINNER). Finish the census, execute the moves, run the predicate once, disclose whatever it returns. The epic ends this wave regardless of exit code. This wins because it is the only direction that can actually END the epic: it treats NO SEAL as a legitimate terminal outcome and moves the honesty into the census (which the predicate cannot express) rather than into the exit code (which cannot express the triage).

RIVAL C — 'Verify the whole apparatus first' vs 'verify only the mechanical preconditions'. A tempting middle path re-proves the predicate, the guard, the roster, and every clause before running — but that over-verification is itself a delay-instrument in disguise. Resolved INTO the winner: verification this wave is SCOPED to the mechanical preconditions the charter already enumerated (GR143 guard-port + warm-standalone, GR149 the three roster traps, GR150 self-orphan travel, GR126 sweep merge daemons + stamp the instant). The predicate is the ONLY substantive judge and it runs last, once. We verify the run CAN happen cleanly; we do NOT re-litigate what it will decide.

The two passages are in tension and this note resolves which one is law.

Grade — A-

No seventh instrument, no widened threshold, no KNOWN_DEFECT added, no predicate edit. Living wave Paper for the Cloud GUI Remake epic (bp task task-47bc4168392dec17, phase 5). Root task this wave: gr-p5r5-successor-seal (the terminal run itself, 13 frozen acceptance criteria). Decide appends the decisions + wave plan BEFORE the builders fly. Review closes this Paper as the debrief. Someone opening this mid-wave sees exactly where it stands. The wish, verbatim

MODEL CONSTRAINT (hard): Fable 5 is spend-limited — every phase runs on Opus/Sonnet, and Decide MUST set builder_model:'opus' for EVERY slice, never 'fable'. — THIS CYCLE: END THE CLOUD GUI REMAKE. Ground truth — re-verified at Strategize (2026-07-21)

The wish's four 'everything is on main' claims were checked at L2 against origin/main and the live ledger. THREE hold; ONE does not, and that gap is the wave's real work.

VERIFIED on origin/main: (1) Clause (b) is SATISFIABLE — the predicate's KNOWN_DEFECTS all carry commit '0261ace15' (seal-predicate.mjs:86/92/98), and git merge-base --is-ancestor 0261ace15 origin/main exits 0. This landed via #5060 (gr-p5r8), not the PR number the wish cites, but the SUBSTANCE is on main. (2) The round-10 DECIDE section (GR142-GR152) is on main via #5089. (3) The named successor cloud-console-hardening-epic resolves PUBLISHED, top-level, open, with its six-band charter and now 7 children (all gr-bl-* backlog rows). The second-successor hazard gr-p5r3-successor-epic reads done. There is exactly ONE forwarding address.

The one wish-claim that does NOT hold — this is the wave's work The '62-row disposition census (#5079)' is NOT yet a written artifact. The charter carries the census PLAN (line 1297, 'Ledger disposition — the census this wave ships') but NOT the 62 individual disposition rows. The census slice gr-p5r10-census is still lifecycle=open at 7/8. And the moves have not happened: the live roster under the epic root reads 140 children {done:80, open:59, in_progress:1}, and the successor has ZERO survivors re-parented (its 7 children are all backlog rows, not forwarded residue). So clause (a) will fail hard (~60 orphans) until this wave executes the move-set. The census and the moves ARE the deliverable; the exit code is only the signature.

The direction — EXECUTE AND DISCLOSE, then END

This is NOT a design wave. There is no new Kinsta/Vercel surface to shape; the CODE that ships the console already shipped. The whole point, learned the hard way across six failed seals, is the META-FINDING: each round spawned a new instrument and the seal receded by one instrument per round. A seventh widening is not rigor — it is how an epic never closes. THIS WAVE BUILDS NO NEW INSTRUMENT. It executes the fully-prepared round-10 plan and takes the verdict.

The finished state this wave delivers: (a) the 62-row disposition census is WRITTEN into the charter — every live row either closed on a named merge SHA or forwarded to the ONE successor with a named band, zero unnamed remainder; (b) the move-set is executed via bp task move (60 orphans to cloud-console-hardening-epic, self-orphan gr-p5r5-successor-seal re-parented LAST, the two in-roster human gates forwarded, cloud-console-billing-live-gate left untouched under its true owner); (c) the frozen predicate runs LAST, ONCE, atomically, by the SAME agent that finished the ledger, from the repo root, with --successor cloud-console-hardening-epic and OVERFLOW_GUARD_PORT set to a verified-free port; (d) its VERBATIM stdout + stderr + exit code + ISO stamp + roster count is recorded in the charter as the TERMINAL ARTIFACT, beside the census and the roster delta — WHICHEVER WAY IT EXITS.

The verdict is disclosure, not rename. The predicate can only measure 'does this row's parent equal the successor id' — a chartered successor and an empty junk-drawer pass it identically. That is why the CENSUS is the real deliverable and the exit code is only the signature. SEAL (exit 0) closes the epic as CODE-sealed. NO SEAL (non-zero) hands the epic to the named successor — a fully pre-authorised, terminal ending. Either way the epic ENDS this wave. There is no round 11.

THE CROWN IS DARK — 'seal' means CODE seal only PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS is unset on the control plane (re-proven live: /v1/me gives platform_operator:false; /v1/operator/warm-pool gives 403). The operator console shipped fully built and remains UNREACHABLE. No commit can set an unset prod env var. The direction debate — the rivals weighed

If the predicate risks a substantive NO SEAL from a real remaining defect, use this wave to also fix it, or to widen the census/measurement so the seal is 'truly' earned. REJECTED: this IS the failure mode that killed six rounds. GR140/GR146 draw the line — widening what the predicate MEASURES (KNOWN_DEFECTS, clauses, thresholds) is the forbidden move; a substantive NO SEAL is not a bug to engineer around, it IS the verdict, and the named successor is the honest ending. A wave that plans to prevent NO SEAL has already lost.

RIVAL B — 'Execute exactly the prepared plan; the census is the deliverable, the exit code is the signature' (WINNER). Finish the census, execute the moves, run the predicate once, disclose whatever it returns. The epic ends this wave regardless of exit code. This wins because it is the only direction that can actually END the epic: it treats NO SEAL as a legitimate terminal outcome and moves the honesty into the census (which the predicate cannot express) rather than into the exit code (which cannot express the triage).

RIVAL C — 'Verify the whole apparatus first' vs 'verify only the mechanical preconditions'. A tempting middle path re-proves the predicate, the guard, the roster, and every clause before running — but that over-verification is itself a delay-instrument in disguise. Resolved INTO the winner: verification this wave is SCOPED to the mechanical preconditions the charter already enumerated (GR143 guard-port + warm-standalone, GR149 the three roster traps, GR150 self-orphan travel, GR126 sweep merge daemons + stamp the instant). The predicate is the ONLY substantive judge and it runs last, once. We verify the run CAN happen cleanly; we do NOT re-litigate what it will decide.

SHARPEST ATTACK on the winner: 'The terminal run happens over a half-moved or mis-mapped roster — greening the predicate over an incomplete triage, or signing a clerical NO SEAL on a self-orphan or a rate-limit false-negative.' HOW THE WAVE ABSORBS IT: GR150 (re-parent self LAST, sub-slices travel as children of a child), GR146 (if census work threatens the run, THE RUN WINS and uncovered rows are named as uncovered — an honest partial census beats a delayed seal), GR126 (atomic, one agent, one instant, stamped), GR149 (status-based rate-limit detection via bp exit 7, never text-matching '429'; roster read ONLY via /v1/data/query filter[parent_id] or bp task get .children, never GET /v1/tasks which silently ignores the filter), and the survey below maps the EXACT current disposition of all ~60 live rows so the terminal-run agent inherits ground truth, not a stale count.

The survey plan — what the fleet scouts before Digest

The survey casts a wide net over the ONE thing this wave cannot execute blind: the current, live, per-row disposition of the roster, plus every mechanical precondition the terminal run depends on. Disclosure questions: (11) is the crown still dark; (12) has the predicate already been run for round 10 (any VERDICT artifact).

What this wave will NOT do

No new instrument, in any disguise. No widening of KNOWN_DEFECTS, clauses, or thresholds. No editing the SEAL banner to make it 'read better'. No re-running the predicate against a widened wave to chase a green. No second successor epic. No touching the surface fence: api/lib/barkpark/tenancy, scripts/pds-*, or api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio (PDS and Studio cycles are RUNNING). Surface fence for edits: cloud/. SURVEY DIGEST — 12 reports in, and the direction's own premise corrected

THE HEADLINE: the Strategize ground-truth correction was itself stale, and this wave is one round of work shorter than planned. The direction asserted that the 62-row census (#5079) is NOT yet a written artifact and that the charter carries only the census PLAN. PR #5079 merged 2026-07-20T20:46:50Z and appended the complete per-row census to .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-gui-remake-charter.md (roughly lines 967-1173): 2 rows CLOSED on named merge SHAs (3f16c9f43, 24fae1b9f), 58 FORWARDED by name across the six named bands of cloud-console-hardening-epic (5/8/15/13/15/2), 1 self-orphan disposed 'by running', zero unnamed remainder.
